title: Steel Battalion
subtitle: Sit down inside the machine

body: Steel Battalion is a combat simulation released for Xbox in Japan on 12 September 2002. The player pilots a Vertical Tank, a heavily armed walking machine, through missions viewed from its cockpit. Its extraordinary controller is part of the game: two sticks, a throttle, switches, pedals and an eject button spread the controls across the player's desk. Rather than condensing the machine into a few familiar inputs, Nude Maker and Capcom made operating it the central activity. Learning where to reach becomes part of learning how to survive.

Each mission begins with a startup procedure. The player brings the tank's systems online before taking it into combat, then manages movement, weapons and the view through its windows. Turning too sharply can topple the machine, while overheating demands another response from the pilot. Even mud on the windscreen has its own control. These details give the cockpit a physical logic: a problem appears in front of the player and a particular switch or action answers it. The controller makes that relationship unusually direct and memorable.

The eject button gives defeat a final decision. If the pilot fails to escape a doomed machine, the character dies and the game deletes the save, making another campaign necessary. New generations of Vertical Tank offer different systems and capabilities as progress continues. Hifumi Kono directed the project and Atsushi Inaba produced it, with Naru Shirai composing the music. The expensive controller and limited production restricted its audience, but they also made Steel Battalion a distinctive example of a game built around a purpose-made piece of hardware.
